Sampling started in South Africa (December 2025, ongoing), with sampling in Namibia recently completed (August 2026), and soon we'll be heading east into the Western Indian Ocean. Sites will be added to the map as they are sampled, so keep an eye on this page to track our progress.

The map below is interactive - feel free to click and explore where we have been.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)
library(rnaturalearth)

# Read study area polygon
# study_area <- st_read("data/study_area.gpkg") |>
#   st_transform(4326)

# 1. Project countries vector
project_countries <- c("Namibia",
                       "South Africa",
                       "Mozambique",
                       "Tanzania",
                       "Kenya",
                       "Seychelles",
                       "Comoros",
                       "Madagascar",
                       "Réunion",
                       "Mauritius")

# Read sampling sites
sites <- read.csv("../data/samplingsites.csv") |>
  st_as_sf(
    coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
    crs = 4326
  )

bbox <- st_bbox(sites)

# 2. Fetch full country geometries to filter lines and labels
country_polygons <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", type = "map_units",  returnclass = "sf") |> 
  filter(name %in% project_countries)

# 3. Download the global coastline layer to subtract it
coastline <- ne_download(
  scale = 50, 
  category = "physical", 
  type = "coastline", 
  returnclass = "sf"
)

# 4. FIX: Convert country polygons into solid outline borders, 
# then completely erase the coastline segments.
inland_borders <- country_polygons |> 
  st_cast("MULTILINESTRING") |> 
  st_union() |> 
  suppressWarnings() |> 
  st_difference(st_union(coastline)) |> 
  suppressWarnings()

# 5. Extract label points ONLY for your project countries
country_points <- suppressWarnings(
  country_polygons |> 
    st_centroid()
)

# 6. Leaflet Map Pipeline
leaflet() |>
  # Satellite imagery
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  
  # SOLID INLAND BOUNDARIES (Guaranteed solid, no coastlines)
  addPolylines(
    data = inland_borders,
    color = "#FFED6F",            # High-contrast color over dark satellite
    weight = 1.5,                  # Thicker line width guarantees visual solidity
    opacity = 0.7,               # Full opacity
    smoothFactor = 1.0,          # Prevents vector distortion at different zoom levels
    group = "Inland Borders"
  ) |>
  
  # Filtered Country Labels
  addLabelOnlyMarkers(
    data = country_points,
    label = ~name,
    labelOptions = labelOptions(
      noHide = TRUE,               
      direction = "center",        
      textOnly = TRUE,             
      style = list(
        "color" = "white",         
        "font-weight" = "bold",    
        "font-size" = "13px",      
        "text-shadow" = "1px 1px 2px black" 
      )
    )
  ) |>
  
  # Zoom to study area
fitBounds(
  lng1 = as.numeric(bbox$xmin),
  lat1 = as.numeric(bbox$ymin),
  lng2 = as.numeric(bbox$xmax),
  lat2 = as.numeric(bbox$ymax)
) |>
  
  # Study area polygon
  # addPolygons(
  #   data = study_area,
  #   color = "white",
  #   weight = 3,
  #   fillColor = "#00BFC4",
  #   fillOpacity = 0.25,
  #   popup = "Study area"
  # ) |>
  
  # Sampling sites
  addCircleMarkers(
    data = sites,
    radius = 6,
    stroke = TRUE,
    weight = 2,
    color = "white",
    fillColor = "#d73027",
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~locality
  ) |>
  
  # Scale bar
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft")
```
